description: Transvaalbuurt 1926-1928 portiek rows of Danie Theronstraat (2-36 and 9-37): a flat-roofed four-storey dark purple-brown brick front over a 1.3 m plain parapet with a thin dark coping (top 13.9 m); the top storey's evenly spaced two-light windows stand between a continuous white sill band (10.25-10.45 m) and a continuous white band 0.5 m over their heads (12.3-12.55 m); on storeys 1-2 the windows come in pairs with white sills, and the stair window, two lights either side of a white mullion, sits over the portiek door under a flat white concrete canopy (3.15-3.3 m). BAG cuts the row into 6 m half-portiek pands (pair + half stair) and 12 m pands (pair, stair, pair); the type is the 6 m half, repeated and mirrored along a 12 m pand

match.note: Danie Theronstraat 2-36 and 9-37 on the 2020-04-29 strips (40 px/m, gridded 1 m): parapet top 13.9-14.2 m (strip skyline 14.1-14.18 on 25D-31A), 3DBAG eaves 12.3-13.1 m read the roof behind the parapet and ridge 15.2-15.8 m the roof-terrace railings, so the eaves are the type's front line (frontEavesM). BAG 1926-1928 on all 21 pands. Frontage: 6 m half-portiek pands (Danie Theronstraat 10-18, 21-31) and 12 m double pands (9-27, 20-30); the 2 m top-storey pitch gives three axes per 6 m. Told from the plain 1928 rows (transvaal-1928-plain-row) by the white bands, which the treed strips do not read (0-1 band runs on 17A-24), so the faces are pinned to this type in transvaalbuurt-west-review-types.json. The corner pands (2-8, 32-36, 33-37: 4.4-11.4 m, eaves 9.7-12.5 m) are other fronts. Axis pitch 1.15-4.1 m: the strip reads the window groups (3 columns over 12 m: pair, stair, pair; 4.0 m) or the windows (5-6 over 6-12 m; 1.2-2.0 m); 0.86 m (12A) is a tree

parapet.note: Danie Theronstraat 25-31 (139446 140487 125668): 1.3 m of plain brick from the white top band to a thin dark coping at 13.9 m; flat roof behind

door-right.note: the portiek door on the stair axis against the party wall under a flat white canopy (3.15-3.3 m, 3-4 m over the double portiek); the garden windows of the ground floor under the window pairs

roof.evidence: Danie Theronstraat 2-37 strips: a level parapet with roof-terrace railings and vent pipes behind it, no roof face over the front; 3DBAG ridge 15.2-15.8 m is the terrace railings and roof storeys set back out of sight

rhythm.bays: per 6 m half-portiek: a window pair (two 1.15-1.25 m two-light windows, 0.35 m pier) and, against the party wall, one half of the stair window; top storey three evenly spaced windows at 2 m pitch
rhythm.identicalBays: no: pairs and the stair window
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: garden windows + portiek door | 1-2: window pair + stair light | 3: three windows between the white bands
rhythm.symmetry: a 12 m portiek unit is symmetric about the stair axis
rhythm.groundFloor: portiek door under a flat white canopy on the stair axis, garden windows and French doors
rhythm.roofline: flat; a 1.3 m plain brick parapet with a thin dark coping over a continuous white band

brick #433d37: per-channel median of the batch wall fit (fit-wall-palette, review wall reading through the city tint) on the six tree-free walls of Danie Theronstraat 17A, 18A, 20, 25D, 29A, 31A (#3b342f-#4c4844); the trim-normalised #6f6058 drew the wall +0.09 lighter. One brick for the row: the per-pand fit on Theronstraat 13A, 16A, 23A, 28 read hedge and tree green (photo blue channel 36-45) and drew olive walls

schemaLimits: the top band's small consoles and the dark header-brick vents over the storey 1-2 pairs are not drawn
the top band is lifted 0.5 m over the top-storey window heads (bandHeights.headLift), as the strip shows
the stair window's white mullion between its two halves is the two pands' frames meeting at the party wall
the French doors of the ground floor are drawn as four-light windows
notes: Palette: the type default is the measured purple-brown of 17A-31A (#716357-#7c6a64); every placed pand takes its trim-normalised strip wall (auto-place measuredPalette).
